_comment: SAMPLE output of `Workflow({ name: 'research-gaps', args })` for the LogScope log-analytics example (docs/examples/log-analytics/). Illustrative, hand-written — shows the exact shape the build step consumes so you can calibrate what 'good' looks like before a real run. Each gap object is passed verbatim as build-gap's args.

gaps.name: Threshold alerts on saved queries
gaps.description: Engineers re-run the same diagnostic query by hand; there is no way to be notified when a saved query crosses a threshold. No alert evaluator, no notification dispatch, no fire history.
gaps.evidence: grep 'alert' across packages/query + packages/api returns only ad-hoc log lines; no AlertRule type; packages/api has no /alerts route; NotificationChannel exists but is only wired to the digest job.

gaps.name: Pre-run query cost / scan estimate
gaps.description: Users fire expensive wildcard queries blind; there is no estimate of bytes scanned or retention-window cost before running, leading to surprise bills and slow dashboards.
gaps.audience: Anyone composing a query in the dashboard or CLI
gaps.evidence: QueryPlan computes a scan range internally (packages/query/src/plan.ts) but never surfaces an estimate; no /estimate route; web query editor has no cost hint; grep 'estimat' = 0 hits in apps/web.

gaps.name: Per-team query scoping (access control)
gaps.description: All authenticated users can query all indices; there is no per-team scoping, so retention/ACL is enforced only at ingest, not at query time. A read path that bypasses team boundaries is a data-exposure risk.
gaps.evidence: QueryPlan.evaluate takes no principal/scope arg (packages/query/src/plan.ts); packages/api auth middleware sets req.user but it is never threaded into the query; no scope tests in __tests__.
